note: Esther names him to his face: 'The adversary and enemy is this wicked man-Haman!' (Esth 7:6), having said 'my people and I have been sold out to destruction' (Esth 7:4).

'So Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.' (Esth 9:29); 'So Esther's decree confirmed these regulations about Purim' (Esth 9:32).

'my people and I have been sold out to destruction' (Esth 7:4). Esth 2:10 is the reason it needs a citation at all: 'Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.'
'Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them' (Esth 9:24). The book calls him this outright rather than leaving it to be inferred.
'he sought to destroy all of Mordecai's people, the Jews, throughout the kingdom of Xerxes' (Esth 3:6), by letters 'to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews-young and old' (Esth 3:13).

'the Jews bound themselves to establish the custom that they and their descendants and all who join them should not fail to celebrate these two days at the appointed time each and every year, according to their regulation.' (Esth 9:27), 'by every generation, family, province, and city' (Esth 9:28).
'Mordecai recorded these events and sent letters to all the Jews ... to establish among them an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar' (Esth 9:20-21).
'there was a certain Jew in Susa the palace, whose name was Mordecai' (Esth 2:5); 'Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Xerxes, preeminent among the Jews' (Esth 10:3).
'he placed the royal crown upon her head and made her queen in place of Vashti' (Esth 2:17) -- the book states the succession in those words.
'His wife Zeresh and all his friends told him, Have them build a gallows' (Esth 5:14) -- the gallows he was hanged on. At Esth 6:13 the same counsellors tell him he shall surely fall.
